findings.title: Read-only RemoteSession role exposes session registration URLs
findings.what: The ClusterRole grants get/list/watch on complete RemoteSession resources. Baseline controller behavior stores the remote-environment registration URL in each resource's status, so users intended only to monitor resources can retrieve a claim-capable authentication URL. The separate status rule does not contain this exposure because Kubernetes get/list on the main resource returns status too.
findings.fix: Do not grant this viewer role access to RemoteSession objects until registration URLs are removed from CR status and stored behind a separately authorized mechanism; then expose only non-sensitive status fields to viewers.
findings.acceptance: Using Kubernetes impersonation for a subject bound only to this role, get/list/watch RemoteSessions must not return any registration or claim URL, while authorized session operators can still obtain it through the dedicated protected mechanism.
findings.verifyNote: An adversarial re-read of the immutable manifest confirmed all three main-resource read verbs. The directly related baseline status-writing code confirms that the full object carries the registration URL; removing only the status-subresource rule would therefore not fix the leak.

findings.title: Manager role has unused cluster-wide node-read privileges
findings.what: The operator ServiceAccount receives get/list/watch for every Node in the cluster. The directly related baseline reconciliation paths do not read, list, watch, or own Node objects, so this exposes cluster infrastructure metadata without a current operational need.
findings.fix: Remove the nodes RBAC rule and its generating RBAC marker; add back only the minimum verb if a demonstrated node-dependent feature is introduced.
findings.acceptance: The rendered manager ClusterRole has no nodes rule, the operator reconciles both custom resources successfully, and an impersonated controller ServiceAccount receives Forbidden when listing nodes.
findings.verifyNote: The immutable lines were re-read in a separate pass. Targeted inspection of the baseline controller setup and reconciliation paths found no Node API use; the only node reference was the permission-generating marker itself.
